what: Title and body start pushed halfway to the right at perspective 1000px (50% − 222.2px, 88px down), tilted 60° on the Y axis and 35° on the X axis and transparent. Once attached, they turn back into place over 1.5s expo.out and stand still. When out is given, as it travels down the screen height × out from the top, they turn back out the opposite way (left −50% + 222.2px, up −120px, −60°·−35°) with sine.in and vanish. A Hero title that turns like walking in through a door.

options.--fx-delay: Wait before entering, default 0s — original subpage body .1s, hero subtitle .3s
options.wait: ready — does not come in until a kf-ready event reaches the document (so it enters after the loader clears). Without it, it enters as soon as attached
options.out: Exit scroll length (multiple of screen height), default none (no exit). Original Hero 0.4
options.lag: How much the exit timeline starts late (share of seconds), default 0 — original subtitle 0.15
options.span: Total length of the outgoing timeline (in seconds), default 0.7 + lag — to keep the title and subtitle on one timeline set both to 0.85
options.y: Distance risen on exit (px), default −120 · original subtitle −200

use: ·

from.where: index.css .hero__title·__subtitle (enter 1.5s expo, subtitle .3s later) · index.js Hero exit (0→.4 screen, .7s sine.in, subtitle .15 later y −200) · shared.css .v-subhero__title·__body (subpage header, body .1s later)

note: The original turns off the transition that comes in on first scroll so it does not fight the scrub — the part does the same. The angle is the same on phone
